edit.description: import the scanners; keep the corpus wiring and the assertions

summary: Move the retired-narration suite's scanner grammars into tests/helpers/ modules, so red-on-base stops carrying each fix forward inside the test file

per.section: A fix ships the test that would have caught it

pins: the retired-narration suite's scanners are imported from `tests/helpers/`, not declared in the suite file
acceptance: the suite is green with every scanner imported, and the pin names the set of scanners it actually found rather than passing over none
notes: Pure move, no behavior change. red-on-base lays the merged bytes of each file holding a named test over the base (`.flume/vitestJudge.ts`); a grammar declared beside its own test rides in that copy, so the line can never be red — two entries reverted on it. The five modules are a prediction; the cut is build's call.

edit.description: widen the tests/ half of the spec locator scan to rootless filenames; retire the doc comment's park

summary: Widen the spec test-cite needle past its tests/ root to a bare *.test.ts filename, leaving the lane's glob

per.section: A claim names behavior, never location

tests: the test-cite needle flags a bare `Dispatcher.test.ts` filename carrying no root
pins: the test-cite needle leaves the `*.integration.test.ts` lane convention unflagged
no spec page cites a bare test filename
acceptance: the widened needle is green over the corpus, and the needle's doc comment no longer parks the rootless half as a human question
notes: Grammar ruled (inbox, 2026-09-11, operator): `*.integration.test.ts` is the lane's marker, so the needle matches a concrete filename and leaves the glob. Green today — `spec/worktrees.md`'s last rootless site was rewritten — and the doc comment deferring the rootless half to a human is expired narration, retired in the same commit. Reverted 9e9b326 is a working implementation. Blocked until the needle leaves the suite file; until then `tests[]` cannot go red.

edit.description: read a single-line doc block's orphan id off its own opener

summary: orphanedBlocks degrades a single-line doc block's id to the empty string; read the id off the opener instead
tests: the orphan scan identifies a single-line doc block by its own text
acceptance: an injected single-line orphan comes back keyed by its text, and two such orphans in one file are two distinct ALLOWED_ORPHANS keys
notes: A single-line block closes on its own opener, so the first-content-line slice is empty and the id falls to `<path>: ` — a placeholder standing in for content that failed to resolve. ALLOWED_ORPHANS is empty today, so the leak is latent: an allowlisted single-line grant would cover any later single-line orphan in the same file. Blocked until `orphanedBlocks` leaves the suite file; until then `tests[]` cannot go red (4dbfc07).
